subject: Discovery recap: FinBot - inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: FinBot - inference cost pressure & next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps so we all have the same page. Please reply if I missed anything.

TL;DR: Primary goal is to reduce inference unit economics while maintaining ML quality and reliability for customer-facing flows. A handful of constraints (latency p95 target, model openness) will drive the recommended path.

Pain points we captured:
- Inference cost pressure: production inference spend has grown ~3x in last 9 months and is now the single biggest line item for your ML infra budget.
- Unpredictable per-token costs across peaks (batching autoscaler not tuned for bursty traffic).
- Latency variability (p95 spikes to ~600ms during morning peaks).
- Current stack fragmentation: in-house Kubernetes serving using Triton for ensemble models + a Redis layer for feature caching. Ops overhead is high.

Current stack & constraints:
- Models: a mix of open LLMs (Llama/Polyglot variants) fine-tuned for domain tasks; willing to try quantized variants if quality holds.
- Infra: GCP (n2-standard + A100s for peak), custom autoscaler, and on-prem inference for sensitive workloads.
- Success criteria: ~40–60% reduction in per-token cost OR ability to scale throughput 2–3x without proportional spend increase; p95 latency <= 300ms for web-facing endpoints; no material drop in top-line QA metrics.

Areas Redwood can help (high-level):
- Unit economics modeling: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization tradeoffs.
- Match runtime kernel selection and autoscaling policies to your traffic shape to avoid cost spikes.
- Private/Dedicated options if you want isolation for sensitive flows.

Agreed next steps:
1) I’ll send our unit-economics template and a short SLA/ops summary (attached) — target: today EOD.
2) Ben (solutions engineer) and Dev (infra lead) to run a short cost-projection exercise: you’ll share two traffic profiles (baseline + peak) and a representative prompt set. (Action: Alex + Priya to send by Wed 12/2)
3) 30-min follow-up demo with a short benchmark of a compatible model variant (can include quantized 4-bit run) — we proposed Thu 12/3 at 11am PT; I’ve included a Calendly link below.
4) We’ll surface quick quality checks on a small eval set you provide to validate quantization effects before larger rollout.

Attachments: redwood-unit-econ-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-sla-summary.pdf (one-pager).

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-2026-1147), schedule (https://cal.com/marissa-redwood/30min).

Thanks — looking forward.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finbot.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinBot - inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 3x increase is mostly from more users + more prompt length (token growth). We can share a representative week from the production logs and a compressed sample of prompts.
- For quantization openness: engineering is comfortable trying 4-bit for non-critical flows; for customer-facing summaries we need an A/B to verify quality.
- Timeline: if we can get a quick cost projection and a benchmark next week that would be ideal — aligns with our Q1 planning.

I’ll send the two traffic profiles and a small eval prompt set by Wednesday (12/2) EOD. Thu 12/3 11am PT works for me for the benchmark demo.

Quick notes on the projection inputs we’ll need:
- Baseline RPS and 95th percentile tokens per request
- Current autoscaler trigger thresholds and typical batch sizes
- A short eval set (50–200 prompts) for quality checks

If anything changes on timing, call it out and we’ll adjust. Looking forward to the demo — Ben will show a quick live run with a quantized candidate and we’ll surface p95 and unit-cost delta in real time.
